entries.not_relevant_because: The family is "A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture", which asks whether closed exact embedded Lagrangians in T*Q are Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section, and it constructs a closed exact Lagrangian in T*(S^9 x S^{N-1}) that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section. It proves no fixed-point count and no Lagrangian intersection bound for a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism (no Betti-number, cup-length or Morse-critical-point lower bound). The only intersection material is background in the introduction (Hofer and Laudenbach–Sikorav constraints on Hamiltonian deformations of the zero section), and the argument never counts L ∩ φ(L). The shared link is only that both are Arnold-type questions in symplectic geometry.
